concept.name: Ascending channel
concept.definition: A channel whose two parallel boundary lines slope upward, enclosing an uptrend's higher highs and higher lows. The lower (support) line connects rising lows and the parallel upper (resistance) line caps the rallies; classically read as trend-consistent structure until broken.
concept.intuition: An uptrend with guardrails: each dip bounces off the lower rail, each push fades near the upper rail.
concept.mechanics: Constructed by drawing an up trendline through two or more rising swing lows and a parallel line through the intervening swing high(s). Range-trading heuristics buy near the lower rail and take profits near the upper; a break below the lower rail warns of trend change.
concept.failure_modes: Upside breaks of the upper rail can be climactic exhaustion moves; downside breaks of the support rail during what looked like orderly ascent catch range traders long at the top rail.
concept.misconceptions: That an ascending channel is purely bullish; a downside break of its support rail is a recognized reversal warning, and rising channels in weak trends often fail downward.
concept.example: A stock's pullbacks bottom on a rising line through 50, 53, 56 while rallies stall on the parallel line through 55, 58, 61 — an ascending channel.
